description: Recorded decisions on where the published spec and bw serve disagree. Detection compares the patched spec's routes with the routes bw serve registers. A difference listed under routes is reported as known; any other needs a decision, and a decision that matches no difference is reported as stale. Behaviour lists differences the route comparison cannot see. Decided on harleypig/bw-serve-client#21.

routes.GET /device-approval/{organizationId}: Registered only by the licensed build (bit-cli). The library offers it, documented as needing that build.
routes.POST /device-approval/{organizationId}/a: Registered only by the licensed build (bit-cli). The library offers it, documented as needing that build.
Registered only by the licensed build (bit-cli). The library offers it, documented as needing that build.
routes.POST /device-approval/{organizationId}/d: Registered only by the licensed build (bit-cli). The library offers it, documented as needing that build.
Registered only by the licensed build (bit-cli). The library offers it, documented as needing that build.

behaviour.GET /object/item-collections/{id}: Documented, but bw serve answers 400. The library does not offer it.

notes: DELETE /object/item/{id} accepts an undocumented `permanent` query. A fix in spec-fixes.json adds it to the patched spec.
Routes are matched ignoring parameter names: bw serve's `{requestId}` is the spec's `{request-id}`.

bw serve registers generic routes such as `/object/{object}/{id}`, so a spec route matches whenever its shape does. An object type a handler rejects, as with item-collections, is a behaviour the comparison cannot see; it is recorded under behaviour by hand.
